theory.intro: Quantities that grow or decay by a constant percentage each period form a **geometric sequence**. If an initial quantity $A_{0}$ changes by a factor of $r$ each time period, the value after $n$ periods is $A_{n} = A_{0} r^{n}$.
facts: For exponential **growth** at rate $p\%$ per period, the common ratio is $r = 1 + \frac{p}{100} > 1$.
For exponential **decay** at rate $p\%$ per period, the common ratio is $r = 1 - \frac{p}{100} < 1$.
In declining-balance depreciation, the salvage value after $n$ years is $V_{n} = V_{0}(1-d)^{n}$ where $d$ is the annual depreciation rate.
The time $n$ required to reach a target value is found by solving $A_{0} r^{n} = T$ using logarithms: $n = \frac{\ln(T/A_{0})}{\ln(r)}$.
steps: Identify the initial quantity $A_{0}$ and the growth or decay factor $r$ per period.
Write the exponential formula $A_{n} = A_{0} r^{n}$ for the quantity after $n$ time periods.
Substitute $n$ to find the future value, or solve $A_{0} r^{n} = T$ for $n$ using logarithms.

foundation.question_text: A bacterial colony has an initial population of $800$ and grows by $15\%$ each hour. Find the population after $4$ hours to the nearest whole number.
A radioactive isotope has an initial mass of $500\text{ g}$ and decays by $20\%$ each day. Find the remaining mass after $3$ days.
A piece of office equipment bought for $\$12\,000$ depreciates by $10\%$ per annum using the declining-balance method. Find its salvage value after $3$ years.

The population of a town is currently $25\,000$ and increases by $4\%$ each year. Write an expression for the population after $n$ years, and calculate the population after $5$ years (to the nearest integer).
A tennis ball is dropped from a height of $200\text{ cm}$. On each bounce, it rebounds to $60\%$ of its previous height. Find the height of the ball at the top of the 4th bounce.
An initial dose of $400\text{ mg}$ of medication is administered. The body clears $25\%$ of the drug every hour. How much drug remains in the body after $2$ hours?
A motorcycle purchased for $\$15\,000$ depreciates at $12\%$ per annum under the declining-balance method. Find the total loss in value during the first year.

development.question_text: A town with population $10\,000$ grows by $6\%$ per year. Use logarithms to find the number of full years needed for the population to exceed $18\,000$.
A new car costs $\$32\,000$ and depreciates at $15\%$ per annum. After how many complete years will its value first fall below $\$10\,000$?
A pond contains $1200\text{ kg}$ of algae. A treatment reduces the algae by $30\%$ each week. Find the amount of algae remaining after $5$ weeks to the nearest kilogram.
A culture of yeast cells doubles in size every $3$ hours. If it starts with $500$ cells, how many cells are present after $15$ hours, and how many hours are needed to exceed $50\,000$ cells?
development.solution_text:
$\text{Periods } n = \frac{15}{3} = 5$
$A_{5} = 500(2)^{5} = 500(32) = 16000\text{ cells}$
$500(2)^{k} > 50000$
$2^{k} > 100$
$k > \frac{\ln(100)}{\ln(2)} \approx 6.64\text{ periods}$
$\text{Time } t = 6.64 \times 3 = 19.93\text{ hours}$
$t \approx 20\text{ hours}$

development.question_text: A drone purchased for $\$4000$ has a salvage value of $\$1024$ after $4$ years under declining-balance depreciation. Find the annual depreciation rate $d$.
A ball is dropped from a height of $16\text{ m}$. If each bounce reaches $75\%$ of the previous height, find the smallest number of bounces $n$ for which the rebound height is less than $1\text{ m}$.
The value of an investment of $\$5000$ increases by $8\%$ per annum compounded annually. Find the doubling time of the investment to the nearest tenth of a year.

mastery.question_text: A transport company buys a truck for $\$80\,000$. Under declining-balance depreciation at $18\%$ per annum, write the recurrence relation for the value $V_n$ and determine the year in which the annual depreciation amount (drop in value over that single year) first falls below $\$5000$.

Two wildlife reserves track their koala populations. Reserve A starts with $120$ koalas and grows at $10\%$ per year ($r_A = 1.10$). Reserve B starts with $300$ koalas and declines at $5\%$ per year ($r_B = 0.95$). Find the number of years after which Reserve A will have a larger koala population than Reserve B.

A cup of boiling water at $100^{\circ}\text{C}$ is placed in a room at $20^{\circ}\text{C}$. The temperature difference $D_n = T_n - 20$ decays geometrically by $12\%$ per minute ($r = 0.88$). Find the temperature after $5$ minutes, and the time taken for the water to cool to $40^{\circ}\text{C}$ (to the nearest minute).
